examples.ko: 농촌 마을이 스스로 자생력을 키워야 해요.
examples.en: Rural villages need to build their own capacity to survive.

examples.ko: 이 풀은 자생력이 강해서 잘 죽지 않아요.
examples.en: This grass is hardy and doesn't die easily.

examples.ko: 작은 가게도 자생력이 없으면 오래 못 가요.
examples.en: Even a small shop won't last long without the strength to stand on its own.

examples.ko: 지원금만 받으면 자생력이 약해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you only rely on subsidies, your self-reliance can weaken.

examples.ko: 지역 경제의 자생력을 높일 방법을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: We are looking for ways to raise the local economy's self-reliance.

examples.ko: 숲은 자생력이 있어서 시간이 지나면 다시 살아나요.
examples.en: A forest can recover on its own, so it comes back to life over time.

explain: 사람, 마을, 회사, 경제처럼 남의 도움 없이 스스로 살아남는 힘을 말할 때 써요. '자생력을 키우다, 기르다, 높이다'처럼 자주 쓰고, 식물이나 숲에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 이 나무는 자생력이 강해서 추운 곳에서도 살아요.
phrases.en: This tree has strong self-sustaining power, so it lives even in cold places.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 살아남는 힘이 크다는 뜻이고 식물에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means strong ability to survive on one's own, also for plants.

phrases.en: Small shops last longer when they become self-sustaining.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 도움 없이 살아갈 힘을 준비한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means preparing the ability to survive without outside help.

phrases.example: 도움이 끊기면 자생력이 부족한 마을은 어려워요.
phrases.en: If aid stops, villages that lack self-reliance have a hard time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 버티는 힘이 약할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the ability to hold out alone is weak.

explain_en: Used for people, villages, companies or economies that can survive without outside help. Common patterns are '자생력을 키우다/기르다/높이다', and it also works for plants and forests.

en: to be arduous; to be extremely difficult

examples.ko: 지난한 노력 끝에 드디어 시험에 합격했어요.
examples.en: After arduous effort, I finally passed the exam.
That task is far more arduous than I thought.

examples.ko: 두 나라가 평화를 이루는 일은 지난할 거예요.
examples.en: Achieving peace between the two countries will be extremely hard.
I recalled the grueling time it took to finish the work.
The trial, which dragged on arduously, ended today.

examples.ko: 이 병을 이기는 일이 지난하다고 의사가 말했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said that beating this illness is extremely hard.

explain: '지난주'의 '지난'과 소리는 같지만 다른 말이에요. 과정이나 노력이 몹시 힘들 때 쓰는 글 말투예요. 말로는 '힘들다', '어렵다'를 써요. 보통 '지난한 과정', '지난한 노력'처럼 명사 앞에 와요.

phrases.en: The road to passing was an arduous process.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말이에요. 끝날 때까지 오래 힘든 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for something that stays hard for a long time.

phrases.example: 그 사람들은 오랫동안 지난한 싸움을 했어요.
phrases.en: Those people fought an arduous struggle for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 힘들게 이어지는 다툼이나 노력에 써요. 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for long, hard struggles; often seen in writing and news.

phrases.en: This work is really hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '지난하다' 대신 '힘들다'를 써요. 훨씬 일상적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, use 힘들다 instead of 지난하다; it's much more everyday.

explain_en: It sounds like the '지난' in '지난주' (last week) but is a different word. It belongs to written style and describes a process or effort that is extremely hard. In speech, people say '힘들다' or '어렵다'. It usually comes before a noun, as in '지난한 과정' or '지난한 노력'.

dis.h: extremely difficult, drawn-out process; written style

p.n: 고되다 stresses tiring toil, while 지난하다 stresses how long and difficult the process is.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 위기에 더 강하게 결속했어요.
examples.en: Our team pulled together more strongly in the crisis.
The citizens united as one and protected the village.

examples.ko: 회원들이 결속하면 큰 힘이 될 거예요.
examples.en: If the members unite, it will be a great strength.

examples.ko: 함께 고생한 일이 우리를 결속하게 했어요.
examples.en: Going through hard times together bound us closer.
The staff went to a workshop on the weekend to bond as a team.
The small countries promised to unite with one another.

explain: 사람들이 한마음으로 단단히 뭉칠 때 써요. 일상에서는 '뭉치다'가 더 자연스럽고, '결속하다'는 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요. 명사로 '결속을 다지다', '결속력'이라는 표현도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: We strengthened our team bond at the company dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결속하다'의 명사 '결속'을 써서 사람들 사이의 단단한 마음을 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It uses the noun 결속 to mean building a firm bond between people.

phrases.en: This club has very strong cohesion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 얼마나 단단히 뭉쳐 있는지를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This describes how tightly a group of people holds together.

phrases.example: 어려울 때일수록 다 같이 뭉쳐야 해요.
phrases.en: The harder things get, the more we all need to stick together.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결속하다'보다 일상적이어서 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is more everyday than 결속하다 and sounds more natural in conversation.

explain_en: It is used when people firmly come together as one. In daily talk '뭉치다' sounds more natural, while '결속하다' shows up more in writing and the news. The noun forms '결속을 다지다' and '결속력' are also common.

dis.h: bind together tightly by a common bond
gh: groups form an alliance or league
join parts or elements into one
casual: band together, or clump up
stand in solidarity for a cause

p.n: 결속 stresses the tight bond; 단결 stresses solidarity for a cause.

examples.en: When the crisis came, the villagers stood together.

examples.ko: 팀이 단결하면 어려운 일도 해낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the team unites, it can accomplish even hard things.
Everyone came together and cheered for our team.
The students joined forces and gave their opinion to the school.
It was really nice to see them stand together.
We will keep standing together as one.

explain: 많은 사람이 한마음으로 힘을 모으는 거예요. 팀, 노동자, 국민처럼 큰 집단에 잘 어울려요. 일상 대화에서는 '뭉치다'가 더 편하고, '다 같이 뭉치자'처럼 말해요. '협력하다'는 일을 함께 하는 것이고, 단결하다는 마음과 힘이 하나가 되는 쪽이에요.

phrases.example: 우리 다 같이 뭉쳐서 이겨 봐요.
phrases.en: Let's all stick together and win.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 친구끼리 말할 때 더 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, and more casual among friends.

phrases.en: My classmates united and finished the cleaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~해서'로 이어서 어떻게 일을 했는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -해서 form says how the work was done.

phrases.en: Our team has strong unity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한마음으로 모이는 힘을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise how strongly a group pulls together.

explain_en: It means many people putting their strength together with one mind. It suits large groups such as a team, workers, or a nation. In casual talk '뭉치다' is easier, as in '다 같이 뭉치자'. '협력하다' is working on something together, while 단결하다 is about hearts and strength becoming one.

dis.h: stand in solidarity for a cause
gh: groups form an alliance or league
join parts or elements into one
casual: band together, or clump up
bind together tightly by a common bond

p.n: 단합 stresses harmony and cooperation rather than firm solidarity.

en: to take care of; to support

examples.en: My mother raised and supported three children on her own.
My parents supported me throughout my life studying abroad.

examples.ko: 남편 공부를 뒷바라지하느라 일을 쉬지 못했어요.
examples.en: I couldn't take a break from work because I was supporting my husband's studies.
Looking after a child's needs isn't easy.
The family who supported the athlete shed tears.
I'd like to support them, but I don't have much money to spare.

explain: 자식이나 가족의 공부, 일을 곁에서 돈과 정성으로 돕는 것을 말해요. 그냥 '돕다'보다 오랫동안 생활 전체를 챙기며 희생한다는 느낌이 있어요. 비슷하게 생긴 '뒷받침하다'는 의견이나 계획을 돕는 데도 써요.

phrases.en: I studied while being supported by my parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도움을 받는 사람의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person being supported.

phrases.en: My wife is busy supporting her husband's studies.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돕는 일 때문에 바쁘거나 힘든 이유를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give the reason someone is busy or tired from supporting someone.

phrases.en: My mother spent her whole life supporting her children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사로 써서 부모가 자녀를 위해 희생하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a noun for a parent's sacrifice for their children.

explain_en: It means helping a child or family member's studies or work from behind with money and care. Compared with plain '돕다', it suggests long-term sacrifice and looking after their whole life. The similar-looking '뒷받침하다' can also support opinions or plans.

en: to make requital; to reward; to return

examples.en: I will surely repay your kindness.
I want to repay my parents' love.

examples.ko: 저는 선생님의 기대에 보답하려고 열심히 공부해요.
examples.en: I study hard to live up to my teacher's expectations.
How should I repay their kindness?

examples.ko: 그 선수는 팬들의 응원에 우승으로 보답했어요.
examples.en: The player repaid the fans' support with a championship.
I bought dinner as a way of saying thanks.

explain: 받은 도움이나 기대에 행동으로 돌려줄 때 써요. '갚다'는 빌린 돈에도 쓰지만 '보답하다'는 감사의 마음이 담긴 점잖은 말이에요. '은혜에', '기대에', '응원에'처럼 '~에'와 함께 써요.

phrases.en: I really want to repay my teacher's kindness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받은 도움과 고마움을 행동으로 갚는다는 뜻으로, 표제어를 '~에'와 함께 쓴 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation: repaying received help and kindness with action, used with '~에'.

phrases.en: I practiced hard to repay the fans' support.
phrases.nuance_ko: 응원해 준 사람들의 마음에 좋은 결과나 노력으로 답할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when answering people's support with good results or effort.

phrases.example: 도와주신 분들께 보답하는 마음으로 일하고 있어요.
phrases.en: I work with a mind to repay those who helped me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보답하다'를 연결형으로 바꿔 어떤 행동의 이유나 태도를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form used to state the reason or attitude behind an action.

explain_en: Use it when you give back, through action, for help or expectations you received. '갚다' also covers borrowed money, but '보답하다' is a more dignified word full of gratitude. It takes '~에', as in '은혜에', '기대에', '응원에'.

en: to support (a family or dependants) financially

examples.en: He supports his parents and younger sibling on his own.

examples.ko: 가족을 부양하려고 두 가지 일을 해요.
examples.en: I work two jobs to support my family.

examples.ko: 정부는 경기를 부양하기 위해 대책을 내놓았어요.
examples.en: The government put out measures to stimulate the economy.

examples.ko: 아들이 나이 드신 어머니를 부양하고 있어요.
examples.en: The son is taking care of his elderly mother financially.
I have many family members to support, so my salary falls short.
My older sister kept supporting our parents even after she married.

explain: 돈을 벌어서 부모나 아이 같은 가족을 먹여 살리는 거예요. 일상에서는 '먹여 살리다'라고도 해요. '키우다'는 아이를 기르는 것이고, 부양하다는 생활비를 책임진다는 쪽이에요. 뉴스에서 '경기 부양'이라고 하면 경제를 일으켜 세운다는 쪽으로 써요.

phrases.en: I have many dependents, so it costs a lot of money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 돈을 벌어 먹여 살려야 하는 가족을 말하는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for family members you must financially support.

phrases.example: 아버지는 혼자 우리 가족을 먹여 살리셨어요.
phrases.en: My father supported our family alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, and more common in daily talk.

phrases.example: 부양할 사람이 많아서 쉴 수가 없어요.
phrases.en: I have many people to support, so I can't rest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~ㄹ'로 꾸며서 책임져야 하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form names the people one must provide for.

explain_en: It means earning money to support family such as parents or children. In daily talk people also say '먹여 살리다'. '키우다' is raising a child, while 부양하다 is about taking responsibility for living costs. In the news, '경기 부양' means boosting the economy.

examples.ko: 이 가수는 팬들에게 멋진 공연을 선사해요.
examples.en: This singer gives her fans a wonderful performance.
I want to treat my parents to a family trip.
An event giving books to children was held.

examples.ko: 큰 웃음을 선사하는 영화라서 자주 봐요.
examples.en: It's a movie that gives you big laughs, so I watch it often.
I secretly prepared a surprise party to give them.

examples.ko: 새해에 회사가 직원들에게 특별 휴가를 선사할 거예요.
examples.en: The company will give its employees special time off for the new year.

explain: '주다'보다 격식 있고 멋진 느낌이라, 선물보다 공연·웃음·감동처럼 기쁜 경험을 줄 때 잘 어울려요. 사람에게 물건을 건넬 때는 '드리다'나 '주다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 그 영화는 관객에게 큰 감동을 선사했어요.
phrases.en: That film gave the audience a deep emotional experience.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기쁜 경험을 줄 때 가장 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The best-fitting pairing for giving a joyful experience.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 늘 사람들에게 웃음을 선사해요.
phrases.en: That actor always brings laughter to people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '웃음을 주다'보다 멋지고 격식 있게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds nicer and more formal than 웃음을 주다.

phrases.en: I want to give my parents a trip as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: '선사하다'와 비슷하지만 일상에서 더 편하게 쓰고 물건에도 잘 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 선사하다 but more everyday, and fits physical gifts too.

explain_en: More formal and polished than 주다. It fits giving a joyful experience such as a performance, laughter or emotion more than handing over an object. For everyday gifts, 주다 or 드리다 sounds more natural.

dis.h: present as a gift or treat
gh: show publicly for the first time

p.s: 그 가수는 팬들에게 멋진 무대를 선사했어요.
p.o: 그 가수는 팬들에게 멋진 무대를 선보였어요.
p.n: 선보이다 just shows it; the gift feeling is lost.

examples.ko: 그 의사는 환자에 대한 인간애가 깊어요.
examples.en: That doctor has deep love for humanity toward his patients.

examples.ko: 인간애를 담은 영화를 보고 눈물이 났어요.
examples.en: I cried watching a film full of humanity.

examples.ko: 재난 현장에서 인간애를 보여 준 사람들이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people showed compassion at the disaster site.
It's a volunteer activity that began out of love for humanity.

examples.ko: 작가는 인간애로 가득한 시를 많이 썼어요.
examples.en: The writer wrote many poems full of love for people.
A society without humanity feels cold.

explain: 특정한 한 사람이 아니라 '사람 전체'를 향한 따뜻한 마음이에요. '박애'와 비슷하지만 더 딱딱한 말이고, 문학이나 뉴스에서 '인간애가 넘치다'처럼 많이 써요.

phrases.en: That movie is full of love for humanity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작품이나 사람에게 따뜻한 마음이 가득할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a work or person is full of warmth toward people.

phrases.en: A stranger helped me, and I felt the warmth of humanity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람의 친절을 보고 따뜻함을 느낄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when kindness from others brings a warm feeling.

phrases.en: They help people in need out of a spirit of universal love.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인간애'와 비슷하지만 더 딱딱한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 인간애 but a stiffer word.

explain_en: It is warm feeling toward people in general rather than one specific person. It resembles '박애' (philanthropy), which is stiffer. In literature and news you see phrases like '인간애가 넘치다'.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 친선 경기를 하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The two countries agreed to play a friendly match.
The purpose of this meeting is goodwill.
It was a friendly tournament, so I enjoyed it without pressure.

examples.ko: 두 학교는 올해부터 친선 교류를 시작했어요.
examples.en: The two schools started a goodwill exchange this year.

examples.ko: 친선 방문으로 도시를 찾은 대표단을 환영했어요.
examples.en: We welcomed the delegation visiting the city on a goodwill trip.
The mayor strengthened ties with the sister city.

explain: '친선 경기', '친선 방문', '친선 대회'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 써요. 이기고 지는 것보다 사이를 좋게 하는 게 목적일 때 써서, 우승을 다투는 정식 경기와 달라요. 친구 사이에는 '친하다'를 쓰고, 친선은 나라·학교·단체 사이에 어울려요.

phrases.en: The president made a goodwill visit to a neighboring country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사이를 좋게 하려고 찾아가는 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A visit made to build good relations.

phrases.en: A friendly tournament will be held this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우승보다 교류가 목적인 대회예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A tournament aimed at exchange more than winning.

phrases.en: I went to the alumni friendship gathering.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사이를 다지려고 하는 모임을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gathering held to strengthen ties.

explain_en: It is used before another noun, as in '친선 경기', '친선 방문' and '친선 대회'. It points to improving relations rather than winning, which sets it apart from an official match. Between friends you say '친하다'; 친선 suits countries, schools and organizations.

examples.ko: 요즘 살림이 군색해서 외식을 못 해요.
examples.en: Money is tight these days, so I can't eat out.
That excuse is too lame.
Even though he was short of money, he always smiled.
His excuse sounded weak.

examples.ko: 군색한 처지가 되어 친구에게 돈을 빌렸어요.
examples.en: I ended up in a tight spot and borrowed money from a friend.

examples.ko: 이유를 대면 댈수록 말이 더 군색해졌어요.
examples.en: The more reasons he gave, the weaker his words became.

explain: 돈이나 형편이 넉넉하지 않아 불편할 때도 쓰고, 변명이나 이유가 억지스럽고 부족해 보일 때도 써요. '가난하다'보다 조금 점잖게 돌려 말하는 느낌이 있어요. '궁색하다'라고도 써요.

phrases.en: Don't make a lame excuse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유가 억지스럽고 부족할 때 '변명' 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before 변명 when the excuse is forced and weak.

phrases.example: 낡은 옷을 입은 모습이 좀 군색해 보여요.
phrases.en: Wearing worn clothes, he looks a bit shabby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이나 형편이 넉넉하지 않아 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone's look or situation seems short of means.

phrases.en: My salary is small, so we're hard up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '살림'과 함께 돈이 모자라 어려운 형편을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with 살림 to describe being short of money.

explain_en: It can describe being short of money and having a hard time, or an excuse that looks forced and weak. It sounds a little more indirect than '가난하다' (poor). It can also be written '궁색하다'.

en: to rake up; to scrape up

examples.en: I raked the fallen leaves together and piled them in one place.
I scraped together my allowance and bought a gift for my friend.
Even if I scrape together all my money, it's not enough.

examples.ko: 흩어진 쌀알을 손으로 긁어모아 봉지에 담았어요.
examples.en: I gathered the scattered grains of rice by hand and put them in a bag.
My friends held a flea market to scrape some money together.

examples.ko: 동전을 긁어모으면 커피 한 잔은 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: If I gather all my coins, I can buy one cup of coffee.

explain: 흩어져 있는 것을 한곳으로 끌어모으는 거예요. 돈을 여기저기서 힘들게 겨우 모았다는 느낌으로도 많이 써요. 정리해서 차곡차곡 모을 때는 '모으다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Even if I scrape together all the money I have, it's not enough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 힘들게 겨우 모았다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling of barely gathering money with difficulty.
phrases.en_equiv: to scrape together all one's money

phrases.en: I raked the snow together with a shovel and piled it to one side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흩어진 것을 끌어서 한곳에 모을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for pulling scattered things into one place.

phrases.en: I gathered the scattered papers in one place.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차곡차곡 정리해서 모을 때는 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural when you gather things neatly.

explain_en: It means pulling scattered things together in one spot. It is also often used for money, with the feeling of barely scraping it together from here and there. For neatly saving up, plain '모으다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: I pulled a chair over and sat by the window.
They bring river water into the fields to farm.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 외국 투자금을 끌어오는 데 성공했어요.
examples.en: This company succeeded in attracting foreign investment.

examples.ko: 줄을 잡고 보트를 해안 쪽으로 끌어왔어요.
examples.en: I held the rope and pulled the boat toward the shore.
He dragged in unrelated topics, and the point became blurry.
I pulled the blanket over me and fell asleep again.

explain: 가까이로 잡아당겨 오게 하는 동작이에요. 의자나 이불 같은 물건뿐 아니라 물, 투자금, 이야기처럼 다른 데 있는 것을 가져올 때도 써요. 오는 방향이 나 쪽이라는 점이 '끌어가다'와 달라요.

phrases.en: It was cold, so I pulled the blanket up to my chin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 내 쪽으로 당길 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic use: pulling an object toward yourself.

phrases.example: 회사가 새 사업을 위해 투자금을 끌어왔어요.
phrases.en: The company brought in investment money for a new business.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 곳에 있는 돈을 가져올 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for bringing in money from somewhere else.

phrases.en: Please don't pull the desk over here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하지 말라고 부탁할 때 쓰는 존댓말 부정 명령형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite negative imperative asking someone not to do it.

explain_en: It means pulling something toward you. Besides objects like chairs and blankets, it is also used for bringing in things from elsewhere, such as water, investment money, or topics. The direction is toward the speaker, unlike '끌어가다'.

examples.ko: 학생들이 어려운 친구를 위해 돈을 모금해요.
examples.en: The students raise money for a friend in need.
There are people collecting donations on the street.

examples.ko: 불이 난 가게를 돕기 위해 모금하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to raise funds to help the shop that caught fire.

examples.ko: 우리 반은 방학 동안 모금하고 나서 쌀을 샀어요.
examples.en: Our class raised money during vacation and then bought rice.
To raise funds, you first need to make a plan.
They dug a well with the money collected at the church.

explain: '돈을 모으다'는 저축처럼 자기 돈도 되지만, '모금하다'는 여러 사람에게 도움이 되는 목적으로 돈을 받아 모을 때만 써요. 돈을 내는 쪽은 '기부하다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 학교에서 어려운 친구를 돕는 모금 활동을 해요.
phrases.en: Our school runs a fundraising drive to help a friend in need.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람에게 돈을 받아 모으는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A drive to collect money from many people.

phrases.en: The neighbors collected donations and delivered them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도움을 위해 낸 돈을 모을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for gathering money given to help someone.

phrases.en: The donations were raised in just one month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모금하다'의 피동형으로, 돈이 모인 결과를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, focusing on the money having been gathered.

explain_en: 돈을 모으다 can mean saving your own money, but 모금하다 is only for collecting money from many people for a shared cause. The side that gives the money says 기부하다.

examples.ko: 말재주만 믿고 준비 없이 발표하면 금방 밑천이 드러나요.
examples.en: If you rely only on your way with words and present without preparing, you'll soon run out of substance.

examples.ko: 작은 가게를 열 밑천을 모으고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm saving up the starting money to open a small shop.
Your body is your capital, so take care of your health first.

examples.ko: 밑천 없이 장사를 시작하는 건 위험해요.
examples.en: Starting a business without any capital is risky.
I opened a restaurant using my severance pay as capital.

examples.ko: 한 번의 실패로 밑천까지 다 잃었어요.
examples.en: I lost even my entire capital in a single failure.

explain: 장사나 일을 시작할 때 드는 돈을 뜻하지만, '몸이 밑천이다'처럼 가진 힘이나 재주를 말할 때도 써요. '자본'보다 말하듯이 편하게 쓰는 느낌이에요. 돈 이야기가 아니어도 '이야기 밑천'처럼 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 시험이 어려워지자 그 학생의 밑천이 드러났어요.
phrases.en: When the exam got harder, that student's true level was exposed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로는 잘하는 척했지만 실제 실력이나 가진 것이 바닥났다는 게 알려질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone who seemed capable is revealed to have little real skill or substance.
phrases.en_equiv: show one's true colors; run out of tricks

explain_en: It means the money needed to start a business or job, but it can also refer to the strength or skill a person has, as in '몸이 밑천이다'. It feels more casual and spoken than '자본'. It can be used for non-money things too, as in '이야기 밑천'.
